citation.title: Chapter 1: Plasma Measurements: An Overview of Requirements and Status
citation.doi_or_arxiv: 10.13182/FST08-A1673 (this paper's own DOI, from the cover page; DOIs in the reference list belong to cited works)

scope_read.limitations: Only the journal version was supplied. PPPL-4276 report pagination cannot be checked and remains unknown. Table text comes from extraction, and some cells are garbled (for example, the Table III n_e temporal cell).

claim_checks.proposed_claim: The edge ion-temperature requirement is 10 ms with 10% accuracy, attributed to FIRE, on p. 288, Table III.
claim_checks.source_finding: Table III lists edge T_i profile requirements: range 0.05-15 keV, 5 mm spatial, 10 ms temporal and 10% typical precision. The listed techniques are CXRS, NPA and optical Doppler spectroscopy. The text says the Table III specifications are those developed for the proposed burning-plasma device FIRE (Ref. 23). It also gives r/a >= 0.8 as the loose geometric edge definition used by ITER and FIRE diagnostic designers.
claim_checks.locator: Table III is on PDF p.10 (journal p.289). The FIRE attribution and edge definition are on PDF p.9 (journal p.288), Sec. II.C.
claim_checks.allowed_intro_sentence: For the edge and pedestal region, measurement-requirement specifications developed for the proposed FIRE burning-plasma device call for ion-temperature profiles at about 5 mm spatial and 10 ms temporal resolution with roughly 10% precision [Young 2008, Sec. II.C and Table III].
claim_checks.qualification: Cite p.288 for the FIRE attribution and p.289 for the table. These are design requirements, not demonstrated performance. The 10 ms figure is a time-resolution requirement, not a computation-latency target. It is not KSTAR-specific and does not address carbon-impurity CES reports.

claim_checks.proposed_claim: Core T_i and rotation requirements are also about 10 ms.
claim_checks.source_finding: Table I lists core T_i (0.5-15 keV) at a/30 spatial and 10 ms temporal resolution with 10% precision. Toroidal and poloidal rotation profiles carry the same a/30, 10 ms and 10% requirements. Sec. II states that the requirements were mostly derived from the most recent ITER set (Ref. 13).
claim_checks.locator: PDF p.7 (journal p.286), Table I; PDF p.5 (journal p.284), Sec. II
claim_checks.allowed_intro_sentence: ITER-derived requirement tables likewise specify ion-temperature and rotation profiles on a 10 ms time scale [Young 2008, Table I].
claim_checks.qualification: Core region is r < 0.8a. Do not merge this with the FIRE edge attribution.

claim_checks.proposed_claim: T_i profiles feed plasma control, which motivates timely estimates.
claim_checks.source_finding: Table VII lists the ion-temperature profile among the measurements for controlling transport-barrier formation and for maintaining the beta profile. Sec. VI says that the need for control often sets the time-resolution requirements in Tables I-VI.
claim_checks.locator: PDF p.18 (journal p.297), Table VII; PDF p.21 (journal p.300), Sec. VI
claim_checks.allowed_intro_sentence: Ion-temperature profiles are among the inputs expected for burning-plasma control, and control needs largely set the quoted time-resolution targets [Young 2008, Table VII; Sec. VI].
claim_checks.qualification: This is the author's expectation for burning-plasma tokamaks. It does not show that nowcasting is useful, and it does not say that CES report latency is a bottleneck.

input_target_timing.inputs: not_applicable (review and requirements paper, not an estimator paper)
input_target_timing.reported_vs_physical_truth: The paper discusses Thomson scattering and ECE disagreeing because of non-Maxwellian electrons (PDF p.3, journal p.282, Sec. I). This can support citing it for the point that measured values depend on the technique used. It does not discuss CES labels.

runtime_or_deployment.what_was_measured: Nothing. Timing figures are required resolutions.
runtime_or_deployment.what_not_established: Achieved latency, report arrival times, real-time T_i estimation, or KSTAR applicability
runtime_or_deployment.locator: Tables I and III; Sec. VI

forbidden_inferences: Treating 10 ms as a demonstrated CES capability or as a computation budget
Attributing Table III to ITER or KSTAR
Claiming the source endorses nowcasting or BES/ECEI-to-T_i estimation
Citing p.288 for the Table III entries
Treating the requirements as validated physics needs
competing_or_complementary: Complementary. The paper supplies requirement context for edge and core T_i time resolution and for diagnostic complementarity. Table II lists BES and ECE for fluctuations, not for T_i.
